source: design-spec-parity-fixtures-4c.md v4 (D2, D3, amendments A1-A4); expected outcomes written by the design's author from the in-progress REM-PARITY text, not generated from the reference
addressing: Faults are given here as physical LBAs of the named image (a filemark counts as a record); the generator records each also as (tape_file, record_index). 'failed_data_addresses' are the (tape_file_number, object_block_index) pairs given to the Recoverer as §13.1 inputs.
record_faults: Record faults (erratum set E1) name one record by tape_file and record_index. 'length' replaces it by a record of that many bytes: the original's leading bytes when shorter, the original followed by zero bytes when longer. 'byte_edits' then set bytes ('set', hex) or XOR them with a mask ('xor', hex) at 'offset' within the record; 'from', when given, is the original bytes there. For the bootstrap (tape file 0, record 0) only, 'payload' replaces the CBOR payload by one the generator builds from the original (a changed 'scheme', 'drive_compression', or the root map's 'key_order'), updating cbor_payload_len and zeroing the old tail if the length changes, and 'header_crc' and 'payload_crc' are 'recomputed', 'stale', or 'recomputed if the length changes'; absent means untouched. The edits apply in that order: length, byte edits, payload, header CRC, payload CRC. A case with 'observations' runs the reader once per observation, each with its own supplied values ('hints'), or none (null). Such a case's 'expected' maps each observation to its outcome; an expectation that reads pending, or that the executor does not know, fails the case.
erratum_e1_source: Expected outcomes of cases e1-01 to e1-15 were written from the REM-PARITY in-progress text (SHA-256 acbc31385e39af233f45769387d7bf33e9a41c38b152a9f8b1cc601c7aa85491) by an author who saw only the text and the constructions, never the reference's outcomes. Every compared field (discovery, error, field, inventory) is transcribed without change, as are the author's sections, quotes and ambiguity notes; the author's reasoning text is omitted and kept with the author's working notes. Each observation's quotes are that text's sentences; a leading bracketed locator names where an excerpt comes from.

A single integer-keyed map (Section 5.3):
When a Reader decodes any CBOR item of this format, it MUST reject duplicate keys and non-canonical encoding, and MUST ignore unknown integer keys at every map level.

supplied values.ambiguity: The text does not define 'decodable'. If it meant decodable under Section 5.3, a Reader rejects the non-canonical item, so no value in it would count as decodable. Row 4 would then give 'continues on the supplied values', error none, and the inventory returned, not degraded. The adopted reading rests on the word 'still' and on the summary sentence (see notes N4 and N5).

quotes: With supplied values, the Scanner judges the first record in two stages: the physical read first and then, for a record of the right length, its content.
a record whose measured length differs from the supplied block size, shorter or longer | refuses it (`BootstrapParse`, naming the block size)
The comparison is always with the supplied block size.

A Reader treats it as invalid content of the component it belongs to: an invalid candidate for a control component, an erasure when the Recoverer reads a data block or parity shard (Section 13.4), and, for the first record with a supplied or known block size, the refusal of Sections 8.4 and 15.
It is never `TapeIo`, which is reserved for a transport or medium failure and for the device reports that Section 2.4 names.
